title: What is the goal of Pokémon FireRed?
content: Pokémon FireRed is a role-playing game in which the player explores towns, routes, caves, and other areas; catches Pokémon; trains them through battles; defeats Gym Leaders to earn badges; progresses through the story; and eventually challenges the Elite Four and the Champion. The main gameplay loop consists of exploration, catching Pokémon, training, battling, and progressing through the region.

title: How do Pokémon battles work?
content: Pokémon battles in FireRed are turn-based. During a battle, the player selects an action such as Fight, Bag, Pokémon, or Run. Fight allows the active Pokémon to use a move. Bag allows the player to use items. Pokémon allows the player to switch the active Pokémon. Run usually allows the player to escape from wild Pokémon battles. In most situations, the Pokémon with the higher Speed stat attacks first.

title: What are the battle menu options?
content: The Pokémon FireRed battle menu contains four main options: Fight, Bag, Pokémon, and Run. Fight is used to select an attack. Bag is used to use items such as Potions and Poké Balls. Pokémon is used to switch the active Pokémon. Run is used to attempt escape from a wild battle and generally cannot be used to escape Trainer battles.

title: What are Pokémon types?
content: A Pokémon type describes an elemental or thematic category, such as Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Rock, or Psychic. Pokémon can have one or two types, and every move has a type. Type matchups determine how effective an attack is against the defending Pokémon. Understanding types is one of the most important battle mechanics in Pokémon FireRed.

title: How does type effectiveness work?
content: In Pokémon FireRed, an attack can be super effective, normally effective, not very effective, or have no effect. A super-effective attack deals 2 times the normal damage. A normally effective attack deals 1 times the normal damage. A not-very-effective attack deals 0.5 times the normal damage. An attack with no effect deals 0 damage. Type effectiveness is determined by the attacking move's type and the defending Pokémon's type or types.

title: What happens when a Pokémon has two types?
content: When a Pokémon has two types, the effectiveness of an attack is calculated against both types. If an attack is super effective against both types, it deals 4 times the normal damage. If it is not very effective against both types, it deals 0.25 times the normal damage. For example, Charizard is Fire/Flying, and Rock-type attacks are super effective against both Fire and Flying, making Rock attacks 4 times effective against Charizard.

title: What is the Fire, Water, and Grass starter triangle?
content: The basic starter type triangle is Fire, Water, and Grass. Fire-type moves are super effective against Grass-type Pokémon. Water-type moves are super effective against Fire-type Pokémon. Grass-type moves are super effective against Water-type Pokémon. This creates a cycle: Fire beats Grass, Grass beats Water, and Water beats Fire.

title: Fire-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Fire-type moves are super effective against Grass, Ice, Bug, and Steel Pokémon. Fire-type moves are not very effective against Fire, Water, Rock, and Dragon Pokémon. Fire-type moves have normal effectiveness against types not listed as weak or resistant. Fire-type Pokémon are weak to Water, Ground, and Rock attacks.

title: Water-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Water-type moves are super effective against Fire, Ground, and Rock Pokémon. Water-type moves are not very effective against Water, Grass, and Dragon Pokémon. Water-type Pokémon are weak to Electric and Grass attacks.

title: Grass-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Grass-type moves are super effective against Water, Ground, and Rock Pokémon. Grass-type moves are not very effective against Fire, Grass, Poison, Flying, Bug, Dragon, and Steel Pokémon. Grass-type Pokémon are weak to Fire, Ice, Poison, Flying, and Bug attacks.

title: Electric-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Electric-type moves are super effective against Water and Flying Pokémon. Electric-type moves have no effect on Ground Pokémon. Electric-type Pokémon are weak to Ground attacks. Electric-type moves are not very effective against Electric, Grass, and Dragon Pokémon.

title: Rock-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Rock-type moves are super effective against Fire, Ice, Flying, and Bug Pokémon. Rock-type moves are not very effective against Fighting, Ground, and Steel Pokémon. Rock-type Pokémon are weak to Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, and Steel attacks.

title: Fighting-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Fighting-type moves are super effective against Normal, Ice, Rock, Dark, and Steel Pokémon. Fighting-type moves are not very effective against Poison, Flying, Psychic, and Bug Pokémon. Fighting-type moves have no effect on Ghost Pokémon. Fighting-type Pokémon are weak to Flying and Psychic attacks. Fairy type does not exist in Pokémon FireRed because it was introduced in a later generation.

title: Psychic-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Psychic-type moves are super effective against Fighting and Poison Pokémon. Psychic-type moves are not very effective against Psychic and Steel Pokémon. Psychic-type moves have no effect on Dark Pokémon. Psychic-type Pokémon are weak to Bug, Ghost, and Dark attacks in Pokémon FireRed.

title: Ghost-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Ghost-type moves are super effective against Psychic and Ghost Pokémon. Ghost-type moves are not very effective against Dark Pokémon. Ghost-type moves have no effect on Normal Pokémon. Ghost-type Pokémon are weak to Ghost and Dark attacks.

title: Dragon-type matchups in Pokémon FireRed
content: Dragon-type moves are super effective against Dragon Pokémon. Dragon-type moves are not very effective against Steel Pokémon. Dragon-type Pokémon are weak to Ice and Dragon attacks. Fairy type does not exist in Pokémon FireRed.

title: What are Pokémon stats?
content: Pokémon have six primary battle stats: HP, Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed. HP determines how much damage a Pokémon can take. Attack affects physical damage. Defense reduces physical damage received. Special Attack affects special damage. Special Defense reduces special damage received. Speed influences which Pokémon attacks first.

title: Physical and Special moves in FireRed
content: In Pokémon FireRed, whether a move is physical or special is determined by the move's type rather than by the individual move. Physical move types are Normal, Fighting, Flying, Poison, Ground, Rock, Bug, Ghost, and Steel. Special move types are Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Psychic, Ice, Dragon, and Dark. Physical moves use the Attack and Defense stats, while special moves use the Special Attack and Special Defense stats.

title: Physical move types in Pokémon FireRed
content: The physical move types in Pokémon FireRed are Normal, Fighting, Flying, Poison, Ground, Rock, Bug, Ghost, and Steel. Damage from these moves is calculated using the attacking Pokémon's Attack stat and the defending Pokémon's Defense stat.

title: Special move types in Pokémon FireRed
content: The special move types in Pokémon FireRed are Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Psychic, Ice, Dragon, and Dark. Damage from these moves is calculated using the attacking Pokémon's Special Attack stat and the defending Pokémon's Special Defense stat.

title: How do Pokémon gain experience?
content: Pokémon gain experience points, commonly called EXP, after participating in battles and meeting the game's experience conditions. When a Pokémon gains enough EXP, it levels up. Leveling up generally increases its stats and may allow it to learn new moves or evolve.

title: How does Pokémon evolution work?
content: Evolution changes a Pokémon into another species, usually making it stronger and sometimes changing its type or abilities. In Pokémon FireRed, Pokémon can evolve through methods such as reaching a certain level, using an evolution stone, or trading. Examples include Charmander evolving into Charmeleon and then Charizard, and Magikarp evolving into Gyarados.

title: How do you catch wild Pokémon?
content: To catch a wild Pokémon in FireRed, the player usually weakens it in battle and then throws a Poké Ball. Lowering the wild Pokémon's HP generally increases the chance of catching it. Certain status conditions, such as Sleep or Paralysis, can also improve the chance of a successful capture. The player can carry up to six Pokémon in the active party.

title: What is a Pokémon party?
content: A Pokémon party is the group of Pokémon currently carried by the player. In Pokémon FireRed, the active party can contain up to six Pokémon. Pokémon that are not in the active party can be stored in the PC system. The player can switch between party members during battles or while exploring, subject to game rules.

title: How do you build a balanced Pokémon team?
content: A balanced Pokémon team should contain different types, moves that cover different weaknesses, and Pokémon that do not all share the same vulnerabilities. Team building involves considering type coverage, move variety, stats, and the roles of individual Pokémon. A player does not need a perfect competitive team to complete the FireRed story.

title: What are Gym Leaders?
content: Gym Leaders are important Trainer opponents in Pokémon FireRed. Each Gym Leader specializes in a particular Pokémon type or battle theme. Defeating a Gym Leader rewards the player with a Gym Badge and usually allows progression through the game. Learning the Gym Leader's type specialty helps the player prepare an effective team.

title: What is the Gym Leader order in Pokémon FireRed?
content: The main Gym Leader order in Pokémon FireRed is Brock, Misty, Lt. Surge, Erika, Koga, Sabrina, Blaine, and Giovanni. Their primary type specialties are Rock, Water, Electric, Grass, Poison, Psychic, Fire, and Ground, respectively. Story events and progression requirements occur between some Gym battles.

title: What are Gym Badges used for?
content: Gym Badges are rewards obtained by defeating Gym Leaders. In Pokémon FireRed, badges allow the player to use certain Hidden Machine moves outside battle and help determine the level of traded Pokémon that will obey the player. Badges also represent progress through the main story.

title: What are TMs and HMs?
content: TMs, or Technical Machines, teach Pokémon specific moves. In Pokémon FireRed, most TMs can generally be used only once. HMs, or Hidden Machines, teach moves that are useful for exploration as well as battle. Important HMs include Cut, Flash, Surf, Strength, Fly, and Rock Smash.

title: What are the important HMs in Pokémon FireRed?
content: Cut allows the player to cut certain small trees. Flash illuminates dark caves. Surf allows the player to travel across water. Strength allows the player to move certain boulders. Fly allows fast travel between previously visited locations. Rock Smash breaks certain rocks. HMs are important for accessing new areas and progressing through the game.

title: What are Pokémon status conditions?
content: Status conditions are effects that can hinder Pokémon during battles. Paralysis can prevent a Pokémon from acting and lowers its Speed. Sleep prevents a Pokémon from acting for a period of time. Poison causes HP loss over time. Burn causes HP loss over time and weakens physical Attack. Freeze usually prevents a Pokémon from acting until it thaws.

title: Why are type matchups important in battles?
content: Type matchups can greatly influence battle outcomes in Pokémon FireRed. A Pokémon with a type advantage can deal increased damage, while a Pokémon attacking into a resistance deals reduced damage. If a matchup is unfavorable, the player can switch to a Pokémon that resists the opponent's moves or use a move with better effectiveness.

title: Beginner tips for Pokémon FireRed
content: A beginner should learn the basic type chart, build a manageable team, carry healing items, save the game regularly, talk to non-player characters for information and items, and explore different areas. Competitive mechanics such as IVs, EVs, and advanced breeding are not necessary to complete the main story. A Pokémon's level, moves, and type advantages are sufficient for a normal first playthrough.

title: How is FireRed different from modern Pokémon games?
content: Pokémon FireRed is based on Generation 3 mechanics. In FireRed, the physical or special category of a move is determined by its type. The Fairy type does not exist. Some mechanics, moves, abilities, and type matchups differ from those in newer Pokémon games. Information intended for FireRed should therefore be distinguished from information about modern Pokémon titles.

title: Example of a super-effective attack in FireRed
content: Suppose the player's Squirtle uses a Water-type move against a Geodude, which is Rock/Ground type. Water is super effective against both Rock and Ground. Therefore, the attack receives a 4 times effectiveness multiplier before other damage calculations are considered. This is an example of a double super-effective matchup.

title: Charizard's type weaknesses in FireRed
content: Charizard is a Fire/Flying-type Pokémon in Pokémon FireRed. It is weak to Water, Electric, and Rock attacks. Rock-type attacks are 4 times effective against Charizard because Rock is super effective against both its Fire and Flying types. Grass-type attacks are not very effective against both of Charizard's types and therefore deal reduced damage.
